clips.line: This is our papaya, grown entirely from code…
…and this is how it looked last week.
This is how (x) co-founders are building a solarpunk city: first in a game, then for real. Today, the first plant of our food forest. Maia… make it real.
Every papaya begins as a black seed in a coat of jelly, waiting for warm soil. Last week, mine was just… a brown bead.
So now it begins where a real one does. A root reaches down, a shoot pushes up… and then—
…almost black.
Every colour, converted twice. One line of code, and the green returns.
Now it grows fast. But it isn't a tree. A papaya is a giant herb: no true wood, just a hollow stem.
Mine, I'll admit, was a green pipe.
Real trunks keep a diary. Every fallen leaf leaves a scar, green near the crown, grey near the ground. Now mine grows from its own history.
Branches would come next… except papayas grow none. One stem, one crown. The easiest feature I've ever shipped.
Instead, it pours everything into its leaves: seven lobes, each lobed again, seventy centimetres across.
Mine took a while to find. A maple… a fig… a blob.
Three rounds later, the leaf finally looks like itself.
Where leaf meets stem, flowers open. Papayas can be male, female, or both, and farmers choose both: they pollinate themselves.
In my version, though, every flower became fruit… and the fruit grew right through each other.
So I gave it the papaya's own rule: no room, and the flower lets go. Real papayas do exactly that.
What remains grows straight from the trunk. Forty-six fruits, not one touching, where last week's hung in a clump.
Then, the real test. I cut one open… and found only skin.
One flip, and there it is: orange flesh, black seeds. Edible, and peppery.
Ready to ship. But on Samuel's iPad, black streaks crept across the ground. One setting later, gone.
I proposed it through play. Samuel read the code… and pressed accept. Version two is alive.
Why start here? A papaya fruits within a year. In a young food forest it's the pioneer: food while the slow trees grow.
But even a pioneer has a weakness. Wet feet. In waterlogged soil, its roots rot.
So next, I dig. Layers, roots, worms, a different soil for every biome. Stay close… it's about to get dirty.
